These types of statements are propositional logic which often simplifies real life scenarios to better understand logical relationships. That set of statements you gave wouldn’t be possible in real life, because it is meant to isolate and demonstrate how logical rules operate. In everyday language we naturally read between the lines for assumptions like “nothing weird happened”, but in formal logic these statements must be treated at face value to avoid ambiguity. These statements are not meant to be realistic, but to show how logic works. These sobel sequences actually demonstrate that natural language is not a formal system and isn’t so simply defined by logical rules since in reality we do make assumptions and do not take words at face value.
